: JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 24072021 at about 6.00 p.m., the Petitioner was driving auto after picking up his passengers from Kittaganuru to Sigehalli and when the petitioner's auto reached near Katamnalluru cross, BengaluruKolar NH75, Brigade signature, at that time, the driver of tempo bearing Reg.No.KA 532001 came in high speed and dashed against the petitioner's auto from back side.
Due to the impact, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries to his legs and other parts of the body.

After the accident immediately, the Petitioner was taken to Government hospital, Hosakote for first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Apollo hospital, Jayanagar, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.

He has spent more than Rs.4,00,000/
towards medical treatment, conveyance and the incidental expenses.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was running auto and was earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

The Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending Tempo and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the Tempo and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 appeared before the court through its counsel.
Respondent No.1 filed objections to the main petition.
Respondent No.2 remained absent, hence placed exparte.

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.1, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tempo.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further, it contended that at the time of alleged accident, the offending vehicle was plied without valid permit and fitness certificate.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

sentences.text: On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 24.07.2021 at about 6.00 a.m. Bengaluru Kolar NH75 road, near Katamnalluru Cross, Bangalore East Taluk, Bangalore, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tempo bearing No.KA532001?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award ?
5. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 15 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.14 & P17.
He also examined a witness as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents as per Ex.P15 and P16 and closed his side evidence.

On the other hand,
the Respondent No.1 got examined three witnesses as RW.1 to RW.3 and got marked Ex.R.1 to R10 and closed its side evidence.

6. The counsel for the respondent No.1 has relied on the decisions reported as under:

Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 24072021 at about 6.00 a.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tempo bearing Regn.No.KA532001.
9.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tempo.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and he also examined a witness as P.W.2 and got marked 15 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P14 & 17.
P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in his chief affidavit.

Ex.P1 to Ex.P9 are the True copies of FIR along with Complaint, Spot Panchanama, Notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Reply notice, IMV Report,
Wound Certificate, Statement of owner of the vehicle, Statement of witnesses and Charge sheet.

Ex.
P.10 is the notarized copy of School transfer certificate, Ex. P.11 is the copy of driving licence, Ex.
P.13 is the Medical bills and Ex.P.14 is the Discharge summary and Ex.P.17 is the certified copies of 4 photographs.

11. Upon going through Ex.P.1 FIR with Complaint, it shows that on the complaint lodged before Avalahalli Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of the Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA53 2001 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 is the Spot Panchanama along with sketch which shows that the same has drawn at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of notice u/s 133 of MV Act.

Ex.P.4 is the copy of reply notice which reflects that as on the date of accident the tempo was driven by a person named Amarnath against whom the police concerned have filed charge sheet after thorough investigation.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV report which shows that accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects.
Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of statement of owner of the vehicle.
Ex.P.8 is the statement of witnesses.

Ex.P9 is the Certified copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Avalahalli Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending Tempo for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
12.
Further, P.W.1 examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as P.W.2 and he reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
13. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.1 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross examination, P.W.1 has denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.1 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.

14. Further, the Respondent No.1 got examined Medical Record Officer by name Rahul as RW.1,
FDA of RTO by name Anand Kumar as RW.2 and also got examined its Manager by name S.Narendran as RW.3 and got marked Ex.R.1 to R.10 and they reiterated the Objection statement contentions in their chief affidavit.
In the cross examination, RW.3 admitted the suggestion that the policy was valid on the date of accident.
He also admits that the DL of the driver of offending vehicle tempo was in force.
He denied the other suggestions of the Learned Counsel for the Petitioner.

Upon careful consideration of the spot mahazar Ex. P.2 and the spot scene sketch, it clarifies that the Harish Kumar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146453534/
4 PW.1/petitioner was driving his auto towards the left side of the road following the traffic rules.

sentences.text: The sketch also reflects the fact that tempo dashed to the auto from behind.
This factor is not in dispute.
Moreover, the IMV report clearly discloses the damages caused to the vehicles.
From the damages caused to the vehicles it can be ascertained that the fact that offending vehicle tempo dashed to the auto from behind which was driven by the petitioner stands proved and justified.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 1 in the 'Affirmative'.
15. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tempo by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 30 years.
He has produced Aadhar card to prove his age.
As per the Aadhar card i.e. Ex.P.12 the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 12.07.1985.
The accident taken place on 24.07.2021.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 36 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
17. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as auto driver and was earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
In this regard, he has produced driving licence to prove his avocation, but he has not produced any supportive documents to show that he was earning Rs.30,000/ p.m.

Therefore, in the absence of any income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2021, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 17,000/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
18.
With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
19.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P6 and other medical records reveal that in the accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Deep lacerated wound (medial) of valar mid foot extending medially approximately 8 cm.
Open wound over dorsum of foot(extending ankle to distal part of mid foot.)
3. Abrasions of 3 x 3 cm.
3. Abrasions of 2 x 2 cm.
In left and right knee aspect of hand.

sentences.text: Deep lacerated wound.
Further, the Doctor has opined that injuries are grievous in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, the injuries do not cause any functional disability to the petitioner.
As such, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

I COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
20.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
21. The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 25.07.2021 to 30.07.2019.
Further, P.W.2 Dr.Nagaraj.B.N has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
22. Upon going through Ex.P.14 Discharge summary which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 25.07.2021 to 30.07.2019 at Apollo Hospital i.e., totally for 6 days.

Therefore,
the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 6 days.
23. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.34,000/ under this head (@ Rs.17,000/ per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
24.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.4,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.4,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.4,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.12,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
25. The Petitioner has deposed that he spent more than Rs.4,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 16 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.13 which is totally amounting to Rs.3,25,590.48/.
The medical bills furnished by the petitioner is not disputed by the respondent No.1.
I have gone through the medical bills and the same are acceptable.
Hence, by rounding of the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,25,600/as a compensation under this head.

sentences.text: VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
26. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and cannot work as earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.
27. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked Clinical notes and Xray at Ex.P.15 and 16.
He assessed physical disability of right lower limbs at 41% and whole body disability at 14%.
28. In the crossexamination PW.2 has admitted that he has not treated the petitioner.
He has also admitted that the there is no fracture.
He has denied the suggestion that without any disability to the Petitioner, he has given higher rate of disability to the Petitioner.

29. Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 10% would be just and proper.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 15.

With multiplier of 15 income of Rs.17,000/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.3,06,000/ (Rs.17,000/ x 12 =
2,04,000/, Rs.2,04,000/x 15 x 10/100 =3,06,000/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,06,000/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
30.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 30,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 12,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs.3,25,600/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 34,000/ laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.3,06,000/ Total Rs.7,37,600/

Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.7,37,600/ with costs and simple interest Harish Kumar vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146453534/
7 at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

sentences.text: 31. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA532001.
The Petition shows the Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
32. ISSUE No. 3 : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.7,37,600/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs. 1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
